title: Structural Studies of ESCRT-III Filaments
content: ESCRT (Endosomal Sorting Complexes Required for Transport) pathways remodel membranes across all three domains of life. All ESCRT pathways feature a conserved class of proteins that form membrane remodeling filaments (termed ESCRT-III filaments in eukaryotes). Most ESCRT-mediated fission events, such as HIV budding, require ESCRT-III filaments to stabilize negatively-curved membranes (the topology found within the bud neck). However, in an increasing number of cases ESCRT-III filaments have been shown to bind and constrict positively curved membranes, including during endosomal vesiculation, at lipid droplet/peroxisome contact sites, and during peroxisomal biogenesis at the ER.
